quiz.explanation: Pakistan's agricultural sector — which employs 38% of the workforce and contributes 19% of GDP — pays almost no income tax because: (1) agriculture is a provincial (not federal) subject, so provinces must tax it, and (2) politically powerful feudal landlords who dominate provincial parliaments ensure agricultural income tax rates are token amounts. This tax expenditure from the agricultural sector (the 'feudal exemption') is estimated at hundreds of billions of rupees annually — a massive subsidy to Pakistan's wealthiest landowners.

laws.title: Supreme Court of Pakistan — Judicial Independence and Crises
laws.subtitle: Pakistan's judiciary navigating between law and political pressure
laws.fullDescription: Pakistan's Supreme Court has had moments of remarkable independence and moments of complicity with executive overreach. Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry's dismissal by Musharraf (2007) triggered the Lawyers' Movement — tens of thousands of lawyers in black suits protesting — restoring him and establishing judicial independence precedent. But the judiciary has also 'validated' coups (law of necessity doctrine), disqualified opposition leaders, and issued controversial political judgments. The PTI-SC dynamic under Imran Khan's ouster and arrest was intensely politicized. The Constitutional Bench Act (2024) created a separate constitutional bench — reducing Chief Justice's solo powers (suo motu jurisdiction). Pakistan's superior judiciary is fiercely contested political terrain.
laws.penalty: Contempt of court: up to 6 months imprisonment under Supreme Court Act. Deliberately disobeying court orders: criminal contempt.
exceptions: Parliamentary privilege protects statements in Parliament from contempt proceedings
Bona fide criticism of judicial decisions (not judges personally) is protected
International organizations and foreign governments have immunity from domestic court orders

quiz.q: What was the Pakistani Lawyers' Movement (2007) and what did it achieve?
options: Lawyers lobbied Parliament to increase judicial salaries
Tens of thousands of lawyers in black suits protested Chief Justice Chaudhry's dismissal by Musharraf — ultimately restoring him and establishing judicial independence precedent
Pakistani lawyers called a national strike demanding an independent anti-corruption court
The lawyers' movement petitioned the UN to declare Pakistan's military courts unconstitutional
quiz.explanation: When General Musharraf suspended Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry in 2007 and imposed emergency rule, thousands of Pakistani lawyers — in their distinctive black coats — took to the streets in one of Pakistan's largest sustained civil society movements. The movement forced Musharraf to restore Chaudhry (after initially refusing), strengthened norms of judicial independence, and became a rare example of civil society successfully constraining military power in Pakistan. The movement contributed to Musharraf's eventual resignation in 2008.

laws.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance — Anti-Corruption in Pakistan
laws.subtitle: NAB's use as political weapon vs. corruption tool
laws.fullDescription: Pakistan's National Accountability Bureau Ordinance (1999) established NAB with sweeping powers: arrest without warrant, detention of up to 90 days without bail, and plea bargaining allowing recovery of assets to avoid prosecution. NAB was created under Musharraf and has been used against political opponents by successive governments. Critics call it a 'political weapon': PTI under Imran Khan used NAB against PPP and PML-N leaders; after Khan's ouster, NAB's powers were reduced by his successors then restored by courts. The abuse of NAB has led to 'political accountability' — prosecuting opponents — rather than genuine corruption fighting. Multiple 'accountability courts' exist. Pakistan's TI CPI score remains poor (~27/100), suggesting NAB has not significantly reduced corruption.
laws.penalty: Corruption/kickbacks: 14 years imprisonment. Willful default on bank loans: 7 years. Assets beyond means (beyond income sources): 14 years. Plea bargaining: repay corruptly acquired assets to avoid prosecution.
exceptions: Court-approved plea bargains allow asset return in exchange for acquittal
Government witnesses who provide evidence against co-conspirators receive immunity
Tax evasion treated separately under FBR — not NAB jurisdiction unless linked to public office

quiz.q: How has NAB (National Accountability Bureau) been criticized in Pakistan's political system?
options: NAB focuses only on small-scale corruption while ignoring billion-dollar corruption
NAB is used as a 'political weapon' — prosecuting opponents of whichever party is in power — rather than as an impartial anti-corruption institution
NAB operates outside judicial oversight, allowing it to imprison people indefinitely
NAB's powers are so weak that no major political figure has ever been convicted
quiz.explanation: NAB's central criticism is that it operates as a selective political tool rather than an impartial anti-corruption institution. When PTI was in power, NAB pursued PPP and PML-N leaders; after PTI's ouster, the new government reduced NAB's powers to limit action against their leaders. Pakistan's TI CPI score (around 27/100) shows that despite decades of NAB activity, corruption has not meaningfully declined — suggesting accountability is political theater rather than systematic anti-corruption. This selective prosecution undermines rule of law.
